description: Small authored review library: guidance, never repository evidence. Not an exhaustive standard or proprietary expertise.

cards.title: Quality scenarios and tradeoffs
cards.principle: Judge a design against a concrete quality goal and its competing costs.
cards.verify: Define a workload or failure scenario, baseline and measurable response; compare a small change with keeping the design.
cards.exception: Static degree cannot establish latency, business impact or a universal severity threshold.
cards.origin: original review checklist inspired by source

cards.title: Cohesion and bounded contexts
cards.principle: Group behavior that shares vocabulary, invariants and reasons to change.
cards.verify: Compare call/state paths, domain terms and change reasons; test one local seam before choosing a deployment boundary.
cards.exception: High degree or several collaborators may be cohesive orchestration; shared atomicity may justify staying together.
cards.origin: original review checklist inspired by source

cards.title: Ports, adapters and dependency direction
cards.principle: Keep application policy testable through explicit boundaries to external technology.
cards.verify: Obtain the allowed dependency rule, trace one violating edge and test the policy through a local port.
cards.exception: A layer name is not a rule; an adapter may intentionally import infrastructure. Avoid interfaces without a useful seam.
cards.origin: original review checklist inspired by source

cards.title: Retries and idempotent effects
cards.principle: Repeated attempts for the same logical operation need an explicit effect and response contract.
cards.verify: Trace request identity and deduplication storage; inject timeouts before and after effects, then repeat the operation.
cards.exception: A retry wrapper alone proves nothing; a local rollback cannot undo an external effect.
cards.origin: original review checklist inspired by source

sources.title: AWS Builders Library: Making retries safe with idempotent APIs

cards.title: State ownership and atomicity
cards.principle: Assign authority for state changes around the invariants that must remain atomic.
cards.verify: Resolve physical stores and actual writers; trace commit boundaries and characterize competing writes before extraction.
cards.exception: A table name is not database identity; reads do not prove shared ownership. A local transaction may be the right boundary.

cards.title: Characterization and architecture checks
cards.principle: Protect observed behavior before changing a structural boundary.
cards.verify: Trace a real call to its state or external effect; test a normal and failure path, then encode the agreed dependency rule.
cards.exception: A test-file link is not coverage; doubles can hide integration failures. Test the contract, not private layout.

cards.title: Architectural decisions and drift
cards.principle: Keep the context and consequences of significant decisions discoverable.
cards.verify: Compare a current accepted decision with cited behavior; record its owner, status, alternatives and a checkable constraint.
cards.exception: A superseded decision or intentional exception may explain a mismatch; document the change before declaring a violation.
cards.origin: original review checklist inspired by source

cards.title: Compatible interface evolution
cards.principle: Separate adding a compatible interface, migrating consumers and retiring the old contract.
cards.verify: Inventory consumers and versions; exercise old/new compatibility, stage one migration and define a rollback checkpoint.
cards.exception: Temporary dual support costs maintenance; an atomic in-process change may be simpler when every consumer is controlled.
cards.origin: original review checklist inspired by source

cards.title: Change and incident triage
cards.principle: Use change patterns to select investigations whose behavior can be checked.
cards.verify: Inspect the commit window, exclude mechanical changes and join explicit incident links before assigning incident impact.
cards.exception: Co-change is correlation; a shared feature or generated files can explain it. Commit authorship alone is not ownership.

cards.title: Trust boundaries and sensitive flows
cards.principle: Verify protections where untrusted input crosses into sensitive state or execution.
cards.verify: Trace a concrete source-to-sink path, authorization and validation; reproduce a rejected unauthorized or malformed request.
cards.exception: A lexical source/sink match is a candidate, not an exploit; framework validation or unreachable paths may disprove it.

cards.title: Operational budgets and observability
cards.principle: Make dependency failure and resource limits observable against an explicit operational budget.
cards.verify: Trace configured timeouts, queue or pool limits and propagation; measure one slow or failed dependency under a stated load.
cards.exception: Declared topology is not a runtime trace; adding retries or queues may amplify load and change delivery semantics.

cards.title: Workflow consistency and compensation
cards.principle: Define valid state transitions and recovery for multi-step effects.
cards.verify: Map one workflow, durable progress and effect order; inject a crash between steps and test restart and duplicate delivery.
cards.exception: Compensation is a new action, not time reversal; retaining one local transaction may be safer than splitting the workflow.
